To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of the plasma membrane Ca2+-ATPase is increased by cGMP, whereas that of the dense tubule Ca2+-AT pump is not.
cGMP increases Vm of the PM Ca(2+),ATPase pump without affecting its Km or Hill coefficient, and that cGMP has no direct effect of the DT Ca2+ accumulating system.
cGMP elevating agents increase the rate of the plasma membrane Ca2+ extruding pump, but do not directly affect the dense tubular Ca2+ accumulating system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that cGMP plays in platelet aggregation.
the effects of cyclic nucleotides (cGMP and cAMP) on Ca2+ transport in human platelets.

the effects of cyclic nucleotides on the kinetics of the platelet plasma membrane (PM), and dense tubule (DT) pumps, and the possible role of these effects in the inhibition of platelet aggregation by agents which elevate cGMP.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibition of platelet aggregation by cGMP is a direct consequence of its ability to increase the rate of the plasma membrane Ca2+ extruding system.
cGMP increases PM Ca2+ pump activity, but does not have any significant effect on DT Ca2+ pump.

cGMP increases [Ca2+]i by accelerating the rate of the plasma membrane Ca(2+)+ATPase and by decreasing the rate of the DT Ca(2+), Mg(2+)+ ATPase, and that cAMP decreases [Ca2+]I by accelerating the rate constants of both pumps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of cAMP and cGMP on the Ca2+-ATPase pump of the PM and on the DT pump of the dense bodies are closely correlated with phosphorylation of the respective proteins by the respective cyclic nucleotide-dependent kinases.
cyclic GMP (cGMP) increases the rate of calcium extrusion pump located at the plasma membrane of human platelets but it does not have any effect on the calcium accumulation system of dense tubules.
the cGMP/cyclic AMP (cAMP) effect on platelet function is mediated through phosphorylation of the PM and DT Ca2+ pumps and the Na+/Ca(2+) exchanger.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cGMP has no direct effect, but only an indirect one, on the Ca2+-accumulating pump of the dense-tubules (DT).
cGMP increases Ca2+ extruding rate of the plasma membrane (the main site of Ca2+ extrudion) but has no direct effects on Ca2+ uptake in the dense tubules.
the cGMP-dependent inhibition of platelet aggregation is not mediated through the dense tubules but through the plasma membrane.
